title: Rajat Patidar Withdraws From India A Squad, Ayush Badoni Named Replacement
excerpt: Patidar told the BCCI he should not be considered for 50-over selection as he manages existing injuries; Badoni joins the squad and Rinku Singh becomes vice-captain.
body:
• Rajat Patidar has told the BCCI he should not be considered for selection in the 50-over format as he manages existing injuries, and has been withdrawn from the India A squad.
  • Ayush Badoni has been added to the squad in Patidar's place, the BCCI said on November 8, 2026.
  • Rinku Singh has been named vice-captain, with Tilak Varma continuing as captain, for the ACC Rising Stars Asia Cup.
  • The tournament runs from November 19 to 29 in Doha, Qatar, and India A open against Nepal on November 20, according to ESPNcricinfo.

Rajat Patidar has withdrawn from the India A squad for the ACC Rising Stars Asia Cup after telling the BCCI that he should not be considered for selection in the 50-over format while he manages existing injuries.

The BCCI said in its November 8 media advisory: "Rajat Patidar has communicated to the BCCI that he should not be considered for selection in the 50-over format as he manages his existing injuries. Accordingly, he has been withdrawn from the India A squad for the ACC Rising Stars Asia Cup."

"Rajat Patidar has communicated to the BCCI that he should not be considered for selection in the 50-over format as he manages his existing injuries."

— BCCI, media advisory, November 8, 2026

Badoni in, Rinku Singh named vice-captain

The Men's Selection Committee has named Rinku Singh as vice-captain, while Ayush Badoni has been added to the squad in Patidar's place, the BCCI said. Patidar had originally been named vice-captain in the Tilak Varma-led squad, according to reporting of the change.

ESPNcricinfo reports that Badoni comes into the side in strong first-class form for Delhi in the Ranji Trophy, with back-to-back double-centuries against Gujarat and against Jharkhand, and that he is currently the second highest run-scorer in the competition with 559 runs from six innings.

Patidar, by contrast, has played three Ranji Trophy games for Madhya Pradesh this season and scored two centuries in them, ESPNcricinfo reports. Before that, it says, he scored two half-centuries in three appearances for India A in the 50-over series at home against Australia A in October. The BCCI statement does not give a return date, and it frames the decision specifically around the 50-over format.

The updated squad

The BCCI's updated India A squad is: Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Prabhsimran Singh (wicketkeeper), Tilak Varma (captain), Rinku Singh (vice-captain), Kumar Kushagra (wicketkeeper), Suryansh Shedge, Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav, Arshad Khan and Ayush Badoni.

ESPNcricinfo notes that the tournament will mark Harshit Rana's return to action. Rana, the 24-year-old fast-bowling allrounder, has not played any cricket since July, when he was with the senior team on the tour of England, it reports. It adds that Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra, currently in New Zealand with the India A red-ball team, will link up with the squad at the end of that tour.

What happens next

The Rising Stars Asia Cup runs from November 19 to November 29 in Doha, Qatar, according to ESPNcricinfo. India A are in Group B along with the UAE, Nepal and Pakistan A, while Group A has Bangladesh A, Sri Lanka A, Afghanistan A and Hong Kong, China, it reports.

India A will face Nepal in their opening campaign match on November 20, and will face Pakistan A on November 22, according to ESPNcricinfo. The top two teams from each group advance to the semi-finals, scheduled for November 26 and 27, with the final on November 29.

For Patidar, the immediate question is left open by the sources: the BCCI has recorded only that he is managing existing injuries and does not want 50-over selection considered for now. No timeline for his return to that format was given in the advisory.
